title: The popular version. He did not give himself an ulcer.
description:
He did not give himself an ulcer. Discover says he developed gastritis, the precursor to an ulcer. The Lasker Foundation says he did not develop an ulcer.

Ulcers were blamed on stress. Scientific American describes the prevailing theory as a psychosomatic illness caused by too much stress. The Lasker Foundation adds excess stomach acid.

Animals would not catch it. The Lasker Foundation reports the bacterium did not grow in animal stomachs, so there was no animal model to prove it.

In July 1984 he drank the broth himself. Discover says he took H. pylori from a patient, stirred it into a broth and drank it. Scientific American says he asked neither an ethics commission nor his wife.

Ten days later, an endoscopy. The Lasker Foundation reports the endoscopy, then a course of antibiotics to clear the infection.

In the 1982 study of 100 patients, 77 per cent of those with stomach ulcers carried H. pylori. The Lasker Foundation reports it.

Shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the bacterium Helicobacter pylori and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcer disease.

He drank the evidence, then took the antibiotics.

Sources:
- https://www.discovermagazine.com/health/the-doctor-who-drank-infectious-broth-gave-himself-an-ulcer-and-solved-a-medical-mystery: read in full. Established that Marshall took H. pylori from a patient, stirred it into a broth and drank it, that he developed gastritis, the precursor to an ulcer, that animals could not be infected, and that Marshall and Robin Warren shared the 2005 Nobel Prize.
- https://laskerfoundation.org/gut-feeling/: read in full. Established the July 1984 swallow, that Marshall did not develop an ulcer, that the bacterium did not grow in animal stomachs, the endoscopy ten days later, the antibiotic course afterwards, the consensus that stomach acid and stress caused ulcers, and that 77 per cent of 100 ulcer patients in the 1982 study carried H. pylori.
- https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/guest-blog/when-scientists-experiment-on-themselves-h-pylori-and-ulcers/: read in full. Established the prevailing theory that ulcers were psychosomatic and stress related, and that he asked neither an ethics commission nor his wife for permission.
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1246068: read in full (BMJ 2005 news item). Established the Nobel citation wording about Helicobacter pylori and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcer disease.
